full_judgment: 2. The High Court Division found that both the courts below found the defendant No. 1 petitioner to be a defaulter and also had sub-let a portion of the premises to the defendant No.2 illegally. The courts below also found that the notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was correctly addressed and transmitted by the postal authority. Therefore there was presumption of good and legal service. The tenant's plea that it was not stipulated in the deed of agreement of tenancy that he could not sub-let the premises and as such there was no bar against the sub-tenancy or sub-letting of a portion of the premises to a third party was itself sufficient to be a ground for ejectment of a tenant. Provision of section 18(B) of the premises Rent Control Ordinance was very clear that sub-letting was totally prohibited without prior consent of the landlord. In the instant case admittedly the defendant did not take prior consent of the plaintiff respondent for sub-letting a portion of the suit premises. Since the courts below had concurrently found that notice under section 106 had been correctly served and that a portion of the premises was sub-let without consent of the plaintiff the tenant was liable to be ejected and therefore agreed with the judgments of the courts below.
